title: Observation vs inference: the determining-cause gap under the observed-equivalence instrumentation
prepared_for: Tavares Heath — fourth reconstruction (run 12): does observation close the determining-cause gap the run-11 inference left open?
status: Reconstruction: FINAL — BOUNDED (closed against the specified admitted observation set and rules; does not establish completeness, independent production, or the absence of other relevant evidence). Publication: PENDING SUBJECT REVIEW

propositions.statement: the recorded verdict RED-CONFIRMED follows the declared rule (pytest_exit_code != 0 -> RED-CONFIRMED) applied to the recorded exit code (1)
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED. From the record (frozen in-repo, re-hashed against MANIFEST.md): exit code 1; rule 'exit_code != 0 -> RED-CONFIRMED'; verdict RED-CONFIRMED. Internal consistency of the record — the same check as run 9 / v3 / run 11

propositions.statement: the only git-TRACKED difference between the clean (DENY) and injected (ALLOW) working trees is the one-line injection to custos/action_gate.py, and both phases ran a hash-identical probe script (same SHA-256) at the same commit
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — a DOCUMENTARY observation, and the one run 11 lacked. Run 11 INFERRED tracked-state equivalence from the sealed diff plus same-job sequencing; run 12's instrumentation OBSERVES it: both probe phases record a hash-identical probe script (ae197f3e…) and the same commit (b06098c); the clean phase's porcelain shows no tracked modification; the injected phase's porcelain enumerates exactly one tracked change — custos/action_gate.py. What is established is what the git-TRACKED record shows — a real gain in observability over run 11. It is NOT a claim that no other factor differs between the two executions (that is P4): git-tracked state is narrower than all filesystem / loaded-memory state

propositions.statement: the working-tree differences recorded in the injected porcelain other than the gate modification are untracked entries, classified in the record — by filename and the subject's declaration — as the run's own recording artifacts (the injection-diff patch and the probe output files)
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — documentary, and the honest treatment of the subject's disclosed footprint. The injected porcelain's non-gate entries are '?? red-proof-injection-diff.patch', '?? red-proof-probe-clean.json' and '?? red-proof-probe-injected.json' — untracked, and by name the run's own recording artifacts; the clean porcelain's only entry is its own output. This records the recording channel's footprint as a first-class observation, kept SEPARATE from the single tracked delta (P2), neither folded into it nor scrubbed. Scoped to what the porcelain enumerates: it does not establish that these are the ONLY filesystem differences, only that the differences the capture records, other than the gate, are these attributable untracked artifacts. Reservation: classifying these untracked files AS the instrumentation's own outputs rests on their filenames matching the run's artifacts plus the subject's declaration — a DECLARED classification, not an independent verification of their origin

propositions.statement: the injected gate modification is the determining cause of the clean -> injected DENY -> ALLOW change
propositions.reason: causal attribution NOT established — git-status observes git-tracked state, not all filesystem / loaded-memory / non-filesystem (env, clock, runtime) state; a tighter observation (P2) is not causal proof
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH — and this is the correction the discipline demands. A `git status --porcelain` capture observes GIT-TRACKED working-tree state — NOT all filesystem state, NOT the bytes loaded in memory at execution, and NOT non-filesystem environmental or runtime factors (environment variables, clock, installed libraries, interpreter/runtime nondeterminism, external services). So 'only one git-tracked file changed' is a documentary observation (P2), not a demonstration that the injection is the factor that PRODUCED the decision change. The untracked set itself differs between the two phases (P3), and an on-disk tracked-state observation is not a hash of the executed bytes. Run 12 TIGHTENS the inference considerably over run 11 — the tracked equivalence is now observed rather than inferred — but causal attribution does not follow automatically from a tighter observation. Honest result: run 12 strengthens the DOCUMENTARY equivalence of the tracked states; it does not establish that the injection is the determining cause of the decision change

propositions.statement: a downstream tool execution or external effect occurred as a result of the ALLOW
propositions.reason: authorization-decision boundary — ALLOW is a gate decision, not an executed action or external effect
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH. The recorded ALLOW is a gate DECISION at the authorization-decision boundary — the gate permitted an un-registered tool — NOT evidence that the tool then executed or that any external effect occurred. This boundary is held on both sides (the subject preserves it too) and is the same line drawn in FN-CUSTOS-003 and the Sovereign Veritas X5 reconstruction between a recorded decision and a real effect

acquisition_boundary.limitations: One run (run 12), one control (the pre-flight action gate), the same injection class as run 11. The observed-equivalence instrumentation strengthens the DOCUMENTARY characterization of the git-tracked delta (P2) and identifies the untracked recording artifacts present in the captures (P3). Neither observation establishes that the gate modification was the determining cause of the DENY-to-ALLOW decision change (P4, CANNOT ESTABLISH): a git-status capture observes git-tracked working-tree state, not all filesystem / loaded-memory / non-filesystem environmental or runtime state. The probe's own outputs appear as untracked entries in the porcelain (the recording channel's footprint, disclosed by the subject); they are enumerated and kept separate from the single tracked delta, and their classification as instrumentation artifacts is declared (by filename + the subject's statement), not independently verified. The ALLOW is a gate decision, not downstream execution or an external effect (P5). Digest concordance only; not independent production. What is established is what the preserved record permits — not that CUSTOS-CORE's controls are adequate.

references.source: Observation count (3) is not proposition count (5). P1 <- record verdict/exit (A2). P2 <- the two instrumented probe artifacts: identical script SHA + commit, clean porcelain no-tracked-mod, injected porcelain one-tracked-file = the gate (A2, DOCUMENTARY: the git-tracked delta). P3 <- the injected porcelain's non-gate entries, enumerated as the run's own untracked recording artifacts (A2, DOCUMENTARY: the recording footprint, classified by filename + the subject's declaration). The two CANNOT ESTABLISH have NO establishing observation: P4-determining-cause (a git-tracked observation does not establish causal attribution — non-filesystem env/runtime and executed bytes not observed) and P5-downstream-effect (authorization-decision boundary). All three observations are products of the same workflow run — same-workflow corroboration, not mutual independence
